newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent weaker.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent weaker.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent weaker Tuesday, based on market orders at 1021 EDT, traders said.
They said follow-through selling could pressure the benchmark December contract to its downside target of 70.00 cents a lb.

NYCE's weekly spec/hedge report showed that the speculators reduced their net long position to 20.5 percent for the week ended July 3, from 21.3 percent the previous week. Analysts said Monday's selloff probably reduced the net position even further.
Monday, speculative selling pressured the most-active month 2.05 cents lower to close at 73.75 cents. The rest board settled down 2.03 to 0.95.
An estimated 28,000 lots changed hands on the day.
USDA reported late Monday that 60 percent of the cotton crop is in good to excellent condition compared with 56 percent a week ago.
NYCE said one notice was issued today, bringing the total to 769 notices issued to date.
